title: Unified Multi-Task Learning & Model Fusion for Efficient Language Model Guardrailing

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to provide LLM guardrailing that avoids the latency, memory, and hosting cost of LLM-based guardrails while beating state-of-the-art detection accuracy. Paper [3] ("LionGuard") shares the same objective of improving LLM safety via guardrails, but it focuses on localized moderation classifiers rather than addressing latency, memory, or hosting costs. Paper [22] ("LLM-Mod") also explores LLM-based content moderation but does not explicitly aim to reduce resource costs or improve detection accuracy beyond state-of-the-art. No prior paper explicitly combines the dual goals of reducing resource costs and achieving superior detection accuracy, making the purpose uncovered.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves fine-tuning sub-1GB classifiers on high-quality task-specific synthetic data produced by a custom guardrail-policy synthetic data pipeline (TaskGuard). Paper [1] ("Synthetic Data Generation with Large Language Models for Text Classification") discusses using LLMs to generate synthetic datasets for text classification tasks, but it does not describe a guardrail-policy pipeline or focus on sub-1GB classifiers. Paper [4] ("Knowledge Distillation in Automated Annotation") uses LLM-generated training labels for supervised text classification but does not involve synthetic data pipelines tailored to guardrail policies. Paper [13] ("Synthetic Data Generation using Imitation Training") proposes synthetic data generation for improving machine learning models but does not describe a guardrail-policy pipeline or sub-1GB classifiers. No prior paper describes a substantively equivalent mechanism, making it uncovered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses public datasets and newly proposed benchmarks (CustomGuardBenchmark) to measure classifier performance against GPT-4 and Aegis-LlamaGuard. Paper [8] ("Benchmarking GPT-4 on Algorithmic Problems") systematically evaluates GPT-4 on various benchmarks, but the evaluation design differs as it focuses on algorithmic problems rather than guardrail benchmarks. Paper [10] ("GPT-4 Technical Report") evaluates GPT-4 on professional and academic benchmarks but does not use guardrail-specific benchmarks. Paper [22] ("LLM-Mod") evaluates LLMs for content moderation but does not use the same benchmark family or validation framework. The evaluation design appears novel, as no prior paper uses the same benchmark family or statistical framework for guardrail-specific validation.

### Domain
The domain is LLM safety/content guardrailing. Paper [3] ("LionGuard") operates in the same domain, focusing on moderation classifiers for unsafe LLM outputs. Paper [22] ("LLM-Mod") also addresses content moderation using LLMs. Both papers work in the general application area of LLM safety/content guardrailing, making the domain covered.

### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to improve guardrail generalization across policies with a single model rather than one model per policy. No prior paper explicitly addresses this objective. Papers like [7] (LoRA-Guard) and [11] (Auditing GPT's Content Moderation Guardrails) focus on guardrails for content moderation but do not aim to generalize across policies with a single model. ### Mechanism
The mechanism involves MultiTaskGuard, a multi-task learning approach performing guardrail-specific pretraining (Guardrail Instruction Pretraining) on a large synthetically generated dataset with unique task instructions, enabling cross-task shared representations. Papers [1], [4], [5], [6], [8], [9], [14], and [19] describe multi-task learning approaches that leverage shared representations across tasks, which is substantively equivalent to the mechanism here. Additionally, [3] (Instruction-based Hypergraph Pretraining) and [12] (Instruction Matters) use instruction-based pretraining, which aligns with the guardrail-specific pretraining described in this contribution. Therefore, the mechanism is covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves comparing MultiTaskGuard's performance against baselines like TaskGuard and RoBERTaLarge, using metrics like average F1 and classification-layer fine-tuning (CFT). Papers [7] (LoRA-Guard), [11] (Auditing GPT's Content Moderation Guardrails), and [21] (Jailbreaking Large Language Models Against Moderation Guardrails) evaluate guardrail performance using similar benchmark setups and metrics, such as classification accuracy and F1 scores. Additionally, [16] (Exploring the Role of Task Transferability in Large-Scale Multi-Task Learning) and [18] (Intermediate-Task Transfer Learning with Pretrained Language Models) use comparable evaluation designs for multi-task learning models. Thus, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is LLM safety/content guardrailing. Papers [7] (LoRA-Guard), [11] (Auditing GPT's Content Moderation Guardrails), and [21] (Jailbreaking Large Language Models Against Moderation Guardrails) explicitly address LLM safety and content guardrailing, making the domain covered.
